coverAlt: A Python machine learning model supplies estimates to Decision Lab’s planning and learning assessments, which return findings to a Python report.

useCase.label: Use-case view
useCase.alt: The analyst supplies shipment inputs, reviews the numerical basis and generates an assessment in the Python shipment application. Maya reads its report to choose a proposal. Actual checking, spending authorization and freight reservation remain outside the application.
useCase.caption: The analyst produces the comparison; Maya uses the report to put forward a shipment proposal. Actual checking, authorization and reservation remain with the responsible people.

components.label: Component view
components.alt: Offline training produces a fitted model for the Python estimator. The adapter calls Decision Lab’s public Python SDK with pinned app definitions. Complete planning eligibility and costs return to the adapter, which binds them with numerical estimates into the information-value assessment. Returned findings feed the Python report renderer.
components.caption: The team’s Python application owns estimation, the bindings and presentation. The public SDK evaluates the pinned app definitions. Complete planning findings return through the adapter as inputs to the information-value assessment.

proposal.alt: The Python report keeps the $6,000 fallback available while the proposed numerical basis awaits review; learning value is not assessed.
proposal.caption: The estimate is a proposed premise. This custom application requires a separate review before calculating learning value.

timely.alt: The qualified timely report proposes checking, with $5,772.96 expected complete cost, $227.04 expected improvement and a 25.0 percent readiness estimate.
timely.caption: The timely $200 check improves expected complete expense under the supplied numerical basis. It establishes no actual registration, purchase or booking.

highFee.alt: With the same estimate, the high-fee report prefers reserving now: the $2,500 check raises expected complete cost to $8,072.96.
highFee.caption: The check can still return in time, but its $2,500 fee outweighs the expected benefit.

late.alt: The late report prefers reserving now because the check leaves no complete response; the learning cost is unavailable rather than a misleading zero.
late.caption: A response ready at 15:00 misses the noon cutoff. The unavailable alternative receives no expected cost.

unsupported.alt: The report withholds a learning estimate for unsupported features while retaining the $6,000 supported fallback.
unsupported.caption: An unsupported estimate does not erase the planning finding or become a zero-probability result.

fee.title: One Python model. Two decision contexts.
fee.sharedBasis: The same fitted Python model, features and numerical proposal feed the same pinned Decision Lab planning and learning apps. Shipment arrangements, recorded permissions, expense and cash boundaries, and the noon reservation cutoff remain unchanged.
fee.change: The Python application supplies a different check fee: $200 or $2,500. The model inputs and the 10:30 a.m. response-ready time stay fixed. Case IDs and titles label the separate scenarios.

panels.label: A $200 check
panels.explanation: Maya can put forward the timely check, retaining Backup if it supplies no usable registration confirmation.

figure.alt: The qualified timely report proposes checking, with $5,772.96 expected complete cost, $227.04 expected improvement and a 25.0 percent readiness estimate.
figure.caption: The timely $200 check improves expected complete expense under the supplied numerical basis. It establishes no actual registration, purchase or booking.

panels.label: A $2,500 check
panels.explanation: The information can still affect the route, but its higher price exceeds the expected improvement. Maya can propose the supported $6,000 fallback now.

figure.alt: With the same estimate, the high-fee report prefers reserving now: the $2,500 check raises expected complete cost to $8,072.96.
figure.caption: The check can still return in time, but its $2,500 fee outweighs the expected benefit.

fee.takeaway: The Python model supplies the same numerical premises. Decision Lab evaluates the changed fee against the available responses and returns a different recommendation to the Python application.

timing.title: The same $200 check. A different time to act.
timing.sharedBasis: The same fitted numerical proposal, complete Direct and Backup arrangements, $9,000 expense and cash boundaries, permissions, and noon reservation cutoff. The chance of registration is about 25%; only actual scoped confirmation can enable Direct.
timing.change: Only the check duration changes, from 120 to 390 minutes. The response still needs 30 minutes, so the complete response is ready at 10:30 a.m. or 3 p.m. Case IDs and titles label the separate scenarios.

panels.label: Ready at 10:30 a.m.
panels.finding: A complete response remains before noon.
panels.explanation: The check can inform the reservation while a supported response remains available.

figure.alt: The qualified timely report proposes checking, with $5,772.96 expected complete cost, $227.04 expected improvement and a 25.0 percent readiness estimate.
figure.caption: The timely $200 check improves expected complete expense under the supplied numerical basis. It establishes no actual registration, purchase or booking.

panels.label: Ready at 3 p.m.
panels.finding: The check leaves no complete response in time.
panels.explanation: Maya can propose Backup now. The late check is unavailable for this decision; its expected cost is withheld.

figure.alt: The late report prefers reserving now because the check leaves no complete response; the learning cost is unavailable rather than a misleading zero.
figure.caption: A response ready at 15:00 misses the noon cutoff. The unavailable alternative receives no expected cost.

timing.takeaway: Information has decision value only when a supported action remains possible after receiving it. The unchanged probability cannot reopen an expired reservation window.
